newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq not to abide by U.N. ban on planes.
newsitem.headline: Iraq not to abide by U.N. ban on planes.

text.p: Iraqi leaders said in a meeting chaired by President Saddam Hussein on Saturday that a United Nations air embargo on Iraq did not prevent it from using its civilian aircraft outside the country.
They said in a statement U.N. resolutions issued after Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait do not bar Iraq from using civilian planes for international flights.

They urged U.N. Security Council members not to follow Washington in its attempt to issue a statement condemning the Iraqi flight on Wednesday of 104 pilgrims from Baghdad to Jeddah, Saudi Arabia and back as a violation of U.N. sanctions.

"Relevant U.N. resolutions, particularly resolution 661 issued on August 6, 1990 and 670 issued on September 25, 1990, do not prevent Iraq from using its planes outside the country," said the statement issued after a meeting of members of the Revolutionary Command Council, Iraq's highest legislative and executive body, and Baath party leaders.

The United States has failed so far to persuade council members to endorse a statement condemning the flight. The U.N. Security Council late on Friday failed to agree on the statement about whether the Iraqi pilgrim flight violated U.N. sanctions.

The official Iraqi News Agency carried the statement, which did not say whether Iraq intended to fly more pilgrims to Mecca in the coming days. It warned Washington against giving different interpretations to the sanctions resolutions.

"A new explanation of resolutions 661 and 670 even in the form of a non-binding presidential statement would be a dangerous precedent which America would try to exploit and give biased interpretations...the thing which Iraq rejects altogether," the statement said.

"American attitude towards this subject is illegal, unfair and biased. The pressure America exerts for the issuing of a stand from the council entails new and biased interpretations of resolutions 661 and 670 and this is unacceptable," it said.
"Iraq shall reject any new interpretation of these two resolutions and all others...and will retain its natural right to use its planes," the statement added.
